data.name: Help_OpeningText
data.value: Use the global hotkey to show or hide WindowDeck. The default shortcut is Win + `. You can change it in Settings. You can also left-click the tray icon to show or hide WindowDeck.

data.name: Help_FindingText
data.value: Type in Search windows to filter by application or visible window/document title. Windows can be grouped by application. When multiple screens are connected, numbered buttons show the current screen and move that exact window to another screen with one click.

data.name: Help_ActionsText
data.value: Click a title or row to activate that exact window. The — button minimizes that window. The × button sends one normal close request to that exact window; the application may still show its usual Save, Don't Save, or Cancel dialog. Group headers provide separate collapse, restore-all, minimize-all, and confirmed close-all actions. Right-click the window list to collapse or expand all application groups.

data.name: Help_PresentationText
data.value:
Presentation Mode helps keep one screen clean while you share it, for example in Microsoft Teams. The selected screen becomes the presentation screen, and the Presentation group is an allow-list of windows that are permitted to appear there. Adding a window to the group does not automatically move it to the presentation screen — it only gives that window permission to remain there.
How to use it: 1. Click Presentation Mode at the bottom of WindowDeck. 2. Click + next to every window that you want to allow on the shared screen. Those windows appear in the Presentation group. 3. Under Presentation screen, select the screen that you intend to share. 4. Under Protection, click Enable. If other windows are already on that screen, WindowDeck shows them before protection is enabled. Move each one to another screen, add it to the Presentation group with +, or use Move all to to move all conflicting windows together. 5. Confirm the dialog. Protection is now active. If another visible window that is not in the Presentation group appears on the presentation screen, WindowDeck automatically moves it to another screen.
The allowed windows do not have to stay on the presentation screen; they may still be used on other screens. Under Protection, click Disable to turn protection off. Turning Presentation Mode off clears the temporary Presentation group and screen selection for that session; windows that were moved are not automatically moved back. Saved window sets and Save current use a native title bar matching the selected light/dark theme. Prepare presentation screen appears above the WindowDeck flyout so you can use its modal controls immediately.

data.name: Help_TrayText
data.value: WindowDeck's X button and Esc hide the flyout. WindowDeck keeps running in the tray. To shut down the application, use Tray > Exit.

data.name: Help_SettingsText
data.value: Settings includes Start with Windows, Start minimized to tray, the configurable global hotkey, grouping by application, application icons, screen numbers, custom Screen numbering with Identify screens, minimized windows, Appearance (System, Light, or Dark), and Language (System, English, or Polski). Maintenance also provides a manual button to review and remove old WindowDeck taskbar icon entries with a backup; the current executable is preserved. In Settings, only the options scroll; OK and Cancel stay visible in a separate fixed footer even with multiple monitors or limited display height.

data.name: Help_AuxiliaryText
data.value: Enable Show auxiliary windows in Settings > Window list to include visible dialogs and floating tool windows with a title. This option is on by default and can be disabled in Settings. Windows with a confirmed owner in the same process appear indented below that owner; use its arrow to collapse or expand the subgroup. Clicking the title activates the selected window. Search temporarily expands matching subgroups and retains the owner as context. Windows without a confirmed visible owner remain separate entries. Embedded or docked panels, untitled windows, and passive helper windows are not included. Close, minimize, move, and Presentation membership still apply to the individual selected window; the application may also affect its owned windows. Collapse state lasts until WindowDeck exits.

data.name: Help_SavedSetsText
data.value: Use Saved sets in the main WindowDeck panel to create multiple named sets. Save current shows all detected windows checked by default; use Select all, Deselect all or individual checkboxes. Later select a saved set and click Open set. Existing windows are not closed. WindowDeck can reopen recognized File Explorer folders and supported local Excel, Word and PowerPoint documents when their real paths can be identified. Browser tabs, unsaved work, virtual folders, and other unrecognized windows are marked as unsupported and cannot be reliably restored. Reopening a set does not restore unsaved changes, exact window positions or internal application state. Sets stay in your local Windows profile and can be renamed, updated or deleted. Saved sets can reopen recognized files and folders. For Notepad, PDF readers and other applications, choose the exact document file in the Save dialog if WindowDeck cannot detect its path. Browser and other program windows without a known document can relaunch the program only, without restoring tabs. For PDF readers or other applications that support one document per window, enable that option in their settings when practical; WindowDeck cannot enforce it. Missing files are reported while remaining set items continue opening. Close set sends normal close requests only to currently open documents and folders whose exact paths can be matched to the selected set. Apps may prompt to save unsaved edits; choosing Cancel keeps that window open. The saved set is never deleted. Program-only entries are skipped to avoid closing unrelated tabs. In tabbed applications a single window can still contain additional tabs, so closing requires confirmation. In Update set, a floppy-disk icon marks windows, documents or folders already saved in the selected set. Those entries are checked by default even when currently closed. Newly opened windows are unchecked and can be selected to add them. Unchecking an entry with a disk icon explicitly removes it only when changes are saved; Cancel leaves the set unchanged. The green check and red X independently show whether the item can be reopened. You can also rename a set within Update set; no separate Rename button is needed.
